question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $y'+2y=0$ for $y\ne0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}y'+2y=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2y \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-2)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int (-2)\,\text{d}x \\ \ln|y| & =- 2 x+C\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

where $K=e^C$ and $K>0.$

We can drop the absolute value bars by allowing $K$ to be either positive or negative. Therefore, the most general solution is

$$
y=K e^{- 2 x}.
